title: Screen solvers by model features

blocks.text: A team keeps a table of what each solver it may use does with each model feature, built the way lesson 5.4.1 built its feature probe. For each solver the table holds two sets of feature names: `"refuses"`, the features the solver rejects with an error, and `"alters"`, the features it accepts but silently changes (as CP-SAT does with continuous variables). Before benchmarking a new model, the team screens the candidates.
Write `screen(features, table)` in `screen.py`. `features` is the set of features the model uses. Return a dict with one verdict per solver in `table`:

items: `"refuses <feature>"` if the solver refuses any feature the model uses, naming the alphabetically first such feature;
otherwise `"alters <feature>"` if it alters any feature the model uses, again the alphabetically first;

blocks.text: A refusal costs a failed run; a quiet change costs a wrong plan. Both rule a solver out, and the verdict names the kind, so a reader knows which one happened. About eight lines.

cases.says: a solver that refuses a feature the model uses gets a refusal verdict, and one that handles everything is ok
a solver that accepts a feature but changes it is not ok either
when a solver both refuses one feature and alters another, the refusal is what is reported
with several refused features, the verdict names the alphabetically first
a solver's gaps in features the model does not use leave it ok

origin.section: Model Features Decide Before Speed Does

concepts: refusals and quiet changes decide which solvers can take a model at all
